pr_comments: I mean this will probably work for him since I doubt the first seat would be his stylus/touchscreen, but I kind of feel like actually handling multi-seat to some extent would be better. I've never bothered with it though so I dunno if there's hidden gory details beyond keep tracking of all the relevant wayland objects and releasing them when needed.

I'm intending to properly implement multi-seat in another PR but it will be a lot more work. AFAIK we can handle it in a way similar to `wl_output` and the work includes:

- keeping a list of all seats
- keeping track of `wl_{keyboard, pointer, touch}` capability and `wl_data_device_manager` for each seat
- mapping between `wl_pointer` and `wl_seat`, needed for interactive resize/move
- mapping between id and `wl_seat` for `global_remove`

For now we can simply receive events from all seats. I'm not sure if it's worthwhile to add a seat filtering option.

The only problem with this is that it will break someone that was hypothetically depending on a device that appears in a later seat. If you wanted to shortcut it, I figure that allowing multiple seats but only one input device type (keyboard, pointer, etc.) globally would be an OK compromise. Of course if you want to implement full multi-seat support, I won't stop you.

> The only problem with this is that it will break someone that was hypothetically depending on a device that appears in a later seat.

True, but I think this shouldn't be a huge problem because pretty much all multi-seat setups are manually configured so they can reconfigure the compositor. Plus the current behavior is already broken (it only uses the capabilities of the last seat advertised) if they depend on devices that appear in the first seat which seems to be more common. 

> I figure that allowing multiple seats but only one input device type (keyboard, pointer, etc.) globally would be an OK compromise.

Implementing this still requires maintaining multiple seat objects, so the work needed won't be less than full multi-seat support while the end result is strictly worse. There is no shortcut if different device types come from different seats even if only one global device per type is allowed. 

If you think this PR is unacceptable in the current form I will convert it later after I get to implement full multi-seat support.

>If you think this PR is unacceptable in the current form I will convert it later after I get to implement full multi-seat support.

I would prefer that tbh so we can solve it the right way.

> I would prefer that tbh so we can solve it the right way.

Done. 

Because the assumption of single seat is so deeply entrenched for the current code, there are lots of global states need to be rewritten for multi-seat conversion. I think I got all of the relevant cases. Let me know if I had missed anything.

issue_context.title: mpv ignores keyboard inputs under sway/wlroots with more than 1 seat configured
issue_context.body:
### Important Information

Provide following Information:
- mpv 0.35.0
- Archlinux
- Tried with the repository version, self-build 0.35.0 as well as mpv-git
- swaywm 1.8 / wlroots 0.16.1
- Intel Corporation HD Graphics 615 / i915

### Reproduction steps

Sway/wlroots allows you to create seats to group input devices together. In my case I wanted to have a separate seat for my touchscreen and stylus.

```
swaymsg seat seat1 attach 1267:9754:ELAN9038:00_04F3:261A_Stylus
swaymsg seat seat1 attach 1267:9754:ELAN9038:00_04F3:261A
```
```
smsg -t get_seats
Seat: seat1
  Capabilities: 5
  Devices:
    ELAN9038:00 04F3:261A
    ELAN9038:00 04F3:261A Stylus

Seat: seat0
  Capabilities: 3
  Devices:
    Microsoft Surface Type Cover Touchpad
    Microsoft Surface Type Cover Mouse
    Microsoft Surface Type Cover
    Microsoft Surface Type Cover Consumer Control
    Microsoft Surface Type Cover Consumer Control
    Logitech MX Master 2S
    Logitech MX Master 2S
    HID 046a:0076
    HID 046a:0076
    HID 046a:0076
    AT Translated Set 2 keyboard
    Intel HID switches
    Intel HID 5 button array
    Intel HID events
    Lid Switch
    Power Button
    Video Bus
```

The problem also occurs if you simply create a new seat for a second keyboard/mouse.

```
swaymsg seat seat_new attach $INPUT_DEVICE
```
Where $INPUT_DEVICE is the device identifier from `swaymsg -t get_inputs`.

The moment the second seat is created mpv stops responding to keyboard inputs.

### Expected behavior
mpv should still respond to keyboard inputs.

### Actual behavior
mpv stops responding to keyboard inputs.

The moment I remove the second seat everything works again.

### Log file
Couldn't find anything related to the issue, you can find the logfile here.
https://0x0.st/oFQy.log
